# Manage workplace safety and emergency readiness

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

When operating premises, employing people in physical work or changing workplace hazards. An owned hazard-control and emergency plan with training, inspections and corrective actions recorded.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. Qualified advisers own legal, tax, safety or regulatory determinations and any required professional work. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Inventory work activities and hazards

agent-runnable


Identify premises, equipment, materials, travel and remote-work arrangements along with people exposed. Capture reported concerns and existing incidents without assuming an office has no safety risks.

- Sources: [OSHA safety and health programs](https://www.osha.gov/safety-management/)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Assess requirements with competent local specialists

human · human approval required


Management and qualified safety advisers determine applicable standards, assessments and responsibilities. Identify urgent hazards and pause unsafe work while required controls are unresolved.

- Sources: [OSHA safety and health programs](https://www.osha.gov/safety-management/)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Approve and implement practical controls

human · human approval required


Assign elimination, engineering, procedural and protective measures appropriate to the hazards. Confirm equipment, emergency access, first-response arrangements and worker consultation with the relevant specialists.

- Sources: [OSHA safety and health programs](https://www.osha.gov/safety-management/)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Train people and exercise emergency procedures

human · human approval required


Workers complete their own instruction and supervised practice where required. Conduct approved drills and checks without exposing participants to uncontrolled hazards.

- Sources: [OSHA safety and health programs](https://www.osha.gov/safety-management/)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Inspect controls and close corrective actions

agent-runnable


Track inspections, equipment maintenance, near misses and worker feedback. Verify fixes with competent owners and reassess when activities, locations or applicable requirements change.

- Verify: An owned hazard-control and emergency plan with training, inspections and corrective actions recorded.
- Sources: [OSHA safety and health programs](https://www.osha.gov/safety-management/)
